verse.text: No temptation has overtaken you except what is common to mankind. And God is faithful; he will not let you be tempted beyond what you can bear. But when you are tempted, he will also provide a way out so that you can endure it.

reflection.scripture: No temptation has overtaken you except what is common to mankind. And God is faithful; he will not let you be tempted beyond what you can bear. But when you are tempted, he will also provide a way out so that you can endure it.
reflection.observation: Paul reminds the Corinthians that temptation is a universal human experience—none of us face something unique or unbearable. The key truth here is God's faithfulness: He doesn't promise a life without temptation, but He guarantees two things—limits on what we face and a way of escape. The phrase 'common to mankind' is comforting because it dismantles the lie that we're alone in our struggles. God's faithfulness isn't passive; He actively provides the way out, often through His Word, His Spirit, or the community of believers around us.
reflection.application: When temptation comes today, pause and remember: you're not the first to face this, and you won't face it alone. Look for the 'way out' God has provided—maybe it's walking away from a conversation, opening your Bible instead of your phone, or calling a trusted friend. The goal isn't perfection; it's endurance through God's faithfulness. Start building the habit of spotting escape routes before you need them.
reflection.prayer: Lord, thank You that You are faithful even when I am not. When temptation feels overwhelming, remind me that You have already prepared a way out. Give me eyes to see it and courage to take it. Help me trust that nothing I face is beyond Your grace, and teach me to lean on Your strength rather than my own. In Jesus' name, amen.
